subject: general
question: How many check-valves are in a tandem master cylinder?

options.text: None; it uses a pump only.
Two, one for front and one for rear brakes

solution:
The correct answer is __Two, one for front and one for rear brakes.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• A tandem master cylinder__ is designed to provide braking for both the front and rear wheels.
 
• It contains two separate circuits — one for the front brakes and one for the rear brakes.
 
• Each circuit has its own check valve, ensuring that the brake fluid does not flow back into the master cylinder.
 
• These check valves maintain pressure in the brake lines for consistent brake performance.
 
• This dual-circuit system enhances safety by ensuring that if one circuit fails, the other can still operate.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Check Valves:**

 
 
• Check valves are one-way valves that allow fluid to flow in only one direction.
 
• They are essential in preventing backflow and maintaining consistent hydraulic pressure.
 
 
 
• **Dual-circuit braking system: **
 
 
• It is designed to enhance safety by separating the hydraulic circuits for front and rear brakes.
 
• Even if one circuit fails, the other circuit can still function, providing partial braking ability.
 
 
 
• **Tandem Master Cylinder:**
 
 
• The tandem master cylinder is a critical component of the dual braking system.
 
• It houses two separate hydraulic pistons, each controlling its own circuit.
